sub: Five criteria, ten points. The exact rubric behind every list we publish.
criteria: Does it sound like a person?
Do we get it in 3 seconds?
Do we know what to do next?
Short lines, smart emoji, no typos.
Does the grid keep the bio's promise?
overview_line: First rule: you must have posted in the last 30 days.

criteria_detail.name: Personality
criteria_detail.question: Does it sound like a real person wrote it?
rules: A line only you could have written
Humour, attitude or a tiny story
Generic adjectives: passionate, quality, best

criteria_detail.name: Clarity
criteria_detail.question: Do we know what you do in three seconds?
rules: Say what you do in the first line
One niche beats five services
Vague taglines with no job in them

criteria_detail.name: Call to action
criteria_detail.question: Do we know exactly what to do next?
rules: One clear action: book, shop, DM
A keyword DM makes it effortless
Three links and no instruction

criteria_detail.name: Details
criteria_detail.question: Is it clean, scannable and typo free?
rules: Short lines, one idea per line
Emoji as signposts, not decoration
Typos, walls of text, personal email

criteria_detail.name: Feed
criteria_detail.question: Does your grid keep your bio's promise?
rules: Sharp, well lit photos of your work
Posted recently and regularly
Blurry shots, random reposts, a dead grid

end_line: Run your bio through the checklist.
checklist: Would a friend recognise your voice?
Is your job in the first line?
Is there one clear next step?

sub: The five things we see most often in bios that never make our lists.
criteria: We can’t tell what you do.
overview_line: Fix one today. Fix all five this week.

criteria_detail.name: No job
criteria_detail.question: If we can’t tell what you do, we scroll on.
rules: A slogan with no job in it
Your service in the first line
One niche beats five services

criteria_detail.name: Buzzwords
criteria_detail.question: Every bio says passionate. Yours should prove it.
rules: Quality, passionate, the best
A date, a number, a fact
Something only you can claim

criteria_detail.name: No next step
criteria_detail.question: A great bio with no action is a dead end.
rules: Three links and no instruction
One clear action: book, shop, DM
A keyword DM makes it effortless

criteria_detail.name: Text wall
criteria_detail.question: Nobody reads a paragraph on a phone.
rules: One block, no breaks
One idea per line
Three or four lines are plenty

criteria_detail.name: No voice
criteria_detail.question: People follow people, not product lists.
rules: A list that could be anyone’s
A tiny story or a real detail
Write like you talk

checklist: Is your job in the first line?
Did you swap one buzzword for a fact?
Is there one clear next step?

sub: Four ways to open a bio, from real accounts in our lists.
overview_line: The first line is the only one everybody reads.

criteria_detail.name: The niche
criteria_detail.question: Lead with what makes you different.
rules: Your specialism, not your category
A number or a promise helps
“Baker” alone. So is everyone.

criteria_detail.name: The hook
criteria_detail.question: Open with a line people want to finish.
rules: A bold statement or a twist
Then explain it in line two
A hook with no follow up

criteria_detail.name: The joke
criteria_detail.question: A little self irony goes a long way.
rules: Laugh at yourself, not at others
Keep the job visible too
An inside joke nobody gets

criteria_detail.name: The promise
criteria_detail.question: Make the reader the hero of line one.
rules: Start with “I help you” or “You”
Name the outcome they want
A promise that could fit any shop
criteria_detail.why: “YOU CHOOSE THE MEANING. I MAKE THE PIECE.”

end_line: Try all four. Keep the best one.
checklist: Does it say what makes you specific?
Would a stranger want to read line two?
Does it sound like you on a good day?

sub: How the best small accounts use emoji to make a bio easier to read.
criteria: One emoji, one kind of info.
overview_line: If you remove the emoji and nothing changes, remove them.

criteria_detail.name: Signposts
criteria_detail.question: Each emoji tells us what the line is about.
rules: Pin for place, box for shipping
Start the line with the emoji
Random sparkles mid sentence

criteria_detail.name: Your symbol
criteria_detail.question: A repeated symbol gives your bio rhythm.
rules: Same bullet on every line
Pick one that fits your brand
A different emoji every line

criteria_detail.name: Identity
criteria_detail.question: One emoji can carry your roots or your niche.
rules: A flag, a tool, a signature dish
Put it next to the word it explains
Five flags, zero meaning

criteria_detail.name: Restraint
criteria_detail.question: Save the emoji for the line that matters.
rules: Plain text, then a pop on the CTA
Two or three in total is plenty
An emoji after every word
criteria_detail.why: ALL THE SPARKLE ON “DM TO BOOK”

end_line: Keep the signs, drop the confetti.
checklist: Is there one that is truly yours?
